ekl1: International threshold for adults up to 50 (4 over 50, 6 in children)
ekl2: It is a simple 9-point examination doctors use to assess joint flexibility: bending the little finger back more than 90 degrees, touching the thumb to the forearm, the elbow and the knee bending backwards more than 10 degrees (one point each for right and left), and placing the palms flat on the floor with the knees straight (one point). Under the 2017 international criteria, the threshold for generalised joint hypermobility is 6 in children and adolescents, 5 in adults up to 50 and 4 over 50. It is not a self-diagnosis test; the diagnosis is made by a doctor.
